name: Subex Ltd
title: Subex Ltd - 532348 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Subex Q4FY26 revenue rose only 3% QoQ to INR 72.96 cr with no numeric FY27 guidance; management leans on 24% order intake growth and a Middle East exposure it calls manageable.

summary.headline: Subex Q4 FY26 revenue rose 3% QoQ to INR 72.96 crores, with EBITDA margin at 14.5% and FY26 order intake up 24%.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was INR 72.96 crores versus INR 70.79 crores in Q3, with EBITDA of INR 10.58 crores (14.5% margin) and normalized PAT of INR 11.51 crores. Management said FY26 full-year total income grew 6% YoY, partly supported by interest income, and that FY25 is not like-for-like because non-core businesses were exited. Order intake grew 24% in FY26 and management highlighted AI deal wins, though it acknowledged top-line growth lagged its ambitions. Middle East exposure, the geopolitical backdrop and slow new-purchase decisions were flagged as the main near-term risks, with revenue conversion expected to improve as implementations finish.

segments.name: Revenue streams: License, Implementation, MS (managed services), AMC
segments.commentary: Management indicated license gross margin is near 90-100%, implementation gross margin 40-45% (up to 60% depending on complexity), MS above 50% and AMC above 70%. These are gross margins before R&D, GTM, G&A and lease costs.

segments.name: Products
segments.commentary: Four core products: Revenue Assurance, Fraud Management, Partner Settlement (wholesale billing) and Enterprise Asset Management. FraudZap is the newer AI fraud product, with one paid customer that onboarded three Telcos through an intermediary.

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: Management said about 31% of revenue comes from the Gulf region, and that APAC and Europe are steady. Africa is seeing momentum and the Americas will get heavy investment in FY27.

guidance_outlook: No formal numerical FY27 guidance was given; management described the team as 'very bullish' and said it expects to beat FY26 results.
Management expects revenue conversion to improve quarter by quarter as implementations of FY26 wins finish, with an uptick expected around the middle of FY27 if there are no delays.
INR 100 crores per quarter revenue was described internally as a target ('war cry'), with no timeline committed.
Management plans to pursue tuck-in acquisitions in FY27, which the board is actively discussing.
Management said the goodwill impairment test is complete and auditors found no impairment needed on carrying value of about INR 190 crores.
capex_capacity: Team of LLMs product has completed POCs and is in talks with two or three customers to go commercial this quarter, but GPU hardware constraints are slowing deployment.
Management is working on running agents on CPU or a laptop-sized 'agent in a box' to get around the GPU constraint; it said it is also looking at neuromorphic hardware.
GenAI-based software development is being embedded across the MCLC to lift developer productivity and reduce engineering cost.
key_quotes: I'll be direct anytime that you ask that question of me.
So, I believe that the reset is done. The foundation is built and FY27 is where we will convert it.
I truly believe that the stock is materially undervalued related to our fundamentals and our trajectory.

financial_highlights.change: +3% QoQ vs INR 70.79 crores in Q3

financial_highlights.value: INR 11.51 crores (13.6% PAT margin as stated)

financial_highlights.change: vs INR 2.9 crores in Q3, which included exceptional items
Management also called it 35% higher than any other year

financial_highlights.value: Strengthened by INR 70 crores over the year
About INR 50 crores after keeping six months of working capital
9 of last 10 quarters; three successive quarters of positive PAT

demand_pricing: Business-as-usual deal sizes are about INR 1-1.5 million; deals above INR 2-3 million are called blockbuster deals and come irregularly.
Middle East deals are being won, but contract signing has been delayed, and new purchase decisions face slower customer decisions. Renewals are described as secure unless the conflict widens.
Customers increasingly ask to pay in local currencies. Subex is sticking to USD, EUR and GBP contracts, which is slowing some negotiations.
Management said the company has about 125-130 active customers, low churn, and about 60% of revenue from top-tier customers.
Management said the company is targeting data centers, mobile money, MVNO, IoT assurance and Telco FinTech as adjacencies, and sees a TAM of about 4.3 million that did not exist two years ago.

qa_highlights.question: Why is order intake not converting into revenue faster, and will Q1 improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said wins are multi-year, so revenue will come as implementations finish. Subscription revenue starts after go-live, and conversion should improve each quarter through FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Middle East exposure and the impact of AI competition?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said work is being moved offshore to Bangalore, renewals look secure, and new wins are the risk. It sees OpenAI-type tools as a tailwind and positions Subex as a system-of-record with an SOI layer on top.

qa_highlights.question: Are the new-product margins and the existing margins different?
qa_highlights.answer: Legacy MS and AMC products carry the margins described earlier. Management declined to give product-level margins because they are competition-sensitive.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Gulf region hit the business and what share of revenue is it?
qa_highlights.answer: A management response put the Gulf share at about 31% of revenue. APAC and Europe are steady. Management said the main risk is delay in new purchases, not renewals.

qa_highlights.question: Is the goodwill write-off a risk?
qa_highlights.answer: The annual impairment test is complete. Auditors found the carrying value is fine and no write-off is needed.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company planning acquisitions or changes to the OnGrid stake?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is discussing tuck-in acquisitions with the board. It is not divesting OnGrid because the investee is doing well and the company has enough cash for its own bets.

risks_watch: Middle East conflict: about 31% of revenue from the Gulf; new-purchase decisions and contract signing could slip further.
Revenue growth remains weak (Q4 +3% QoQ; FY26 total income +6% YoY, partly from interest income). Watch whether Q1 FY27 conversion improves.
GPU hardware constraint may delay commercialization of Team of LLMs and agent products.
Receivables from a closed sectorial contract are being pursued through legal action and arbitration, with timing uncertain. Provisions already exist.
Management declined to share milestone-based payment schedules, which limits visibility into revenue timing of large deals.
Currency: customers are pushing for local-currency contracts, which the company is resisting.
summary.management_tone: Confident and bullish about FY27 and the AI product pipeline, but cautious on the Middle East and on conversion timing. Management acknowledged revenue growth has been slower than it wanted, and gave no numerical guidance when asked.

growth.why: No numeric FY27 guidance; management is 'very bullish' and expects to beat FY26, backed by a 24% FY26 order intake and conversion uptick mid-FY27, but no specific capacity or contracted timing is given and the Middle East and new-purchase delays are flagged as risks.
